full_judgment:
10. Mr. M. Bazlur Rahman Talukder, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellants, submits that order of conviction is not based on any legal testimony and as such it is not sustainable. It is further submitted that material witnesses have been withheld to prove alleged recovery of the gun from the possession of the appellants and in absence of such proof the conviction cannot stand. It is further submitted that procedure laid down in section 103 of the CrPC relating to conduct of search was not observed by the informant and because of non-observance of the procedure laid down in section 103 CrPC the recovery of alleged arms cannot be said to have been proved. It is further submitted that alleged arms were not examined by arms expert and as such it does not come within the mischief of definition of Arms specified in section 19A of the Arms Act and no independent witness has been examined in this case though such witnesses have been named in the FIR Ext. 1. 

 11. Informant Shahadat Hossain who is also o/c of the thana has deposed in this case as PW 1. He stated in his evidence that on 4.11.80 at about 11-30 he got a secret information from one person named Babul that appellants have been in possession of unauthorised SBBL gun and on getting such information be rushed to the spot and recovered the gun from the possession of the appellants. But he did not say in his evidence who was present at the time of recovery of the alleged gun and that procedure for search of the gun as laid down in section 103 of the CrPC was followed by him or not The alleged gun was also not produced in Court during trial. This informant is highly interested in the result of this case and as such his testimony unless corroborated' by independent and unimpeachable evidence, no reliance can be placed on it. 

 13. No other independent witness has been examined in this case though names of 4 witnesses have been mentioned in the FIR. It appears from FIR Ext. 1 that 4 persons namely Mukhter, Md. Shahjahan, Maniruddin and Nurul Islam were present when alleged search was conducted in the house of the appellants but none of the above named persons has been examined in this case as witness. It surpasses my comprehension how order of conviction can be based on the uncorroborated testimony of the informant (PW 1) who is a police officer and is vitally interested in the result of the case. It is not known why prosecution withheld independent witness whose names appear in the FIR Ext. 1. Further the arms alleged to have been recovered from the appellants was also not examined by arms expert to ascertain whether it is in working condition and it falls within the mischief of the Arms Act as defined in section 19A of the Arms Act. The evidence of PW 1 Shahadat Hossain is tainted with interestedness and bias because he is a police personnel and is vitally interested with the result of the case. It is not understood how order of conviction can be based on a tainted evidence of PW 1 alone. Further it is not understood why the alleged gun was not produced in court during trial. 

 14. Having considered this fact, circumstances and evidence on record, I am of the opinion that order of conviction is not sustainable in law and it is accordingly set aside.
